what.text: This page follows people displaced inside Georgia by conflict and violence, counted by IDMC and by UNHCR and shown side by side.
At the end of 2025, IDMC estimated 300549 people in internal displacement, and UNHCR counted 300439.
Refugees from Georgia live mainly in France and Germany.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over South Ossetia territory, between the government of Georgia and the Republic of South Ossetia, in 2004 and 2008.
The sources here don't say what caused the displacement that UNHCR first counted in 1993.
Mass movements are the disasters recorded for Georgia in IDMC's data.

when.text: IDMC's figure stayed between 206600 and 300549 from 2009 to 2025, changing very slowly since 2018.
UNHCR's figures for people displaced inside Georgia go back to 1993, and IDMC records no new displacements from conflict in these years.

how.text: In 2025 IDMC counts 110 more internally displaced people than UNHCR; the figures overlap and are never added.
The sources don't say where inside Georgia people live.
